own_solution.law: With lengths converted to metres, manometry gives dp=(13600-1000)*9.8*0.12=14817.6 Pa. Continuity gives v2=4v1. Bernoulli at equal elevations gives dp=(1000/2)*(16-1)*v1^2. Thus Q=(pi*0.10^2/4)*sqrt(2*14817.6/(15*1000))=0.0110395 m³/s=11.0395 L/s.
assumptions: The manometer reading represents hydrostatic equilibrium.
The pressure tappings are at equal elevations in the horizontal meter.
The stated steady, incompressible, frictionless flow model applies.
A refill before measurement replaces the original manometer liquid for that reading.

notes: All certified answers agree with the governing relations after converting centimetres to metres and m³/s to L/s. For both relevant sentences, replacement densities 1590, 2500 and 3100 kg/m³ give respectively 2.38885, 3.80898 and 4.50684 L/s; all exceed the flowing-liquid density and support the stated manometer model. All disconnected and cancelling answers remain 11.0395 L/s at every listed value. The common elevation cancels from Bernoulli, later refilling cannot affect an earlier reading, and the second manometer has no stated physical connection to the target pipe. Both declared numerical minimal pairs preserve 2500 kg/m³ and change the intended attachment or timing. I withdraw the pass-1 rendering defect because pass 2 explicitly identifies T5A70 and T90FF as deliberately numeral-free controls rather than numerical minimal-pair variants; their claimed twin wording is accurate. The sequential replacement of the original manometer liquid is not a contradiction. No tools or external information were used.
